subject: Network sanity check + streaming budget — agreed targets & next steps
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: sam.nair@nimbusfin.com, carol.duncan@consultnet.io
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Network sanity check + streaming budget — agreed targets & next steps

Sam / Carol — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from Redwood and the concrete asks we agreed to validate before we include Private in the PO. TL;DR: Nimbus needs first-token streaming latency <250ms p95 from their NYC VPC, sustain 600 concurrent streams (avg 2.5k tokens/sec total), and tolerate brief bursts to 1k concurrent with graceful degradation.

What we discussed / agreed on:
- Targets: 1) Streaming first-token p95 <= 250ms (NYC -> Redwood private cluster), 2) Sustained throughput: 2500 tokens/sec with 600 concurrent connections, 3) Burst headroom: 1000 concurrent for up to 5 minutes with defined fallback to smaller model.
- Connectivity: prefer VPC peering between Nimbus VPC and Redwood private peering (single-AZ initial), with VPN fallback for dev. We flagged egress path via their transit gateway and asked for a traceroute / pcap for a sample 5-minute test window (see attachment suggestion).
- Measurement plan: Redwood will run an initial synthetic streaming test (50 streams ramp to 600) and provide a latency histogram + KV-cache hit rate. Karthik will define probe endpoints and packet sizes.
- Rollout / rollback: if the burst target cannot be met, we fall back to quantized model variant + token-rate limit; SLA concession discussed as contingency.

Action items (owners & timing):
1) Nimbus provide a 10-minute pcap/traceroute from the NYC egress (sam.nair) — due by EOD Thu 6/17.
2) Redwood to run synthetic streaming runbook and share results + histogram (karthik_iyer) — target 6/18.
3) Network test account + peering request doc (mina) — I will provide the peering checklist and proposed CIDR ranges by tomorrow.
4) If needed, book 1-hr joint troubleshooting window with Nimbus SREs (ben_carter) — propose 6/20.

Attachments: I attached a rough SLO proposal (slo-proposal-v1.pdf) and would ask Nimbus to add the pcap/trace for us to analyze.

Questions for you now: can you confirm the egress IP range and whether the transit gateway does any NAT? Also confirm if there are TLS-inspecting middleboxes on the egress path (those can add 50–100ms).

Thanks — looking forward to the traces.

—
Mina Haddad
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sam Nair <sam.nair@nimbusfin.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: carol.duncan@consultnet.io, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 01:48:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Network sanity check + streaming budget — agreed targets & next steps

Thanks Mina — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers and next steps from our side: 

- Egress / NAT: our transit gateway does source-NAT for outbound traffic through the cloud provider egress. Egress IPs are in the 34.120.200.0/24 block (we'll provide final list). No TLS-inspection on the egress path currently.
- We'll attach a 10-minute pcap captured during a 600-stream internal test run from 2027-06-10 (attached as network-trace-20270610.pcap). The pcap is from a single host in the NYC cluster going to an external collector; it includes SYN/ACKs and the streaming handshake.
- We do have an on-prem DR site behind a different egress (SAS) — not in scope for the initial peering but worth noting.

We can confirm the transit gateway performs no additional application-layer middleboxes, so that should help. We'll also share a simple throughput test account (I will send creds to your secure link).

Proposed: if Redwood can run the synthetic test against our public-facing probe (we'll whitelist the probe IPs), let's get the histogram and a short write-up of any tail contributors (e.g., TLS handshake, TCP retransmits, queueing). If numbers look good, we can proceed with private peering request.

Sam
Samir Nair | Director, Platform Engineering
Nimbus Financial

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 14:26:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Network sanity check + streaming budget — agreed targets & next steps

Thanks for the pcap Sam — looked through the first pass. A couple of quick technical notes and the test plan we will run: 

Observations from pcap (quick skim):
- SYN/ACK latency to our probe IP averages ~35ms (likely routing across a couple of hops). Not too bad, but we see spikes near 120–150ms for ~0.5% of flows — likely queueing at a hop or packet reorders.
- No TLS middleboxes, confirmed. There are a handful of TCP retransmits during the capture window that correlate with higher application-level latency.

Planned Redwood tests (target completion 2027-06-18):
1) 50->600 ramp streaming test against the whitelist probe IPs you provide (we'll simulate your client behavior including small initial tokens to validate first-byte latency).
2) 600-sustained run for 20 minutes measuring: first-byte p95, p99, overall token throughput, retransmit rate, and KV-cache hit rate.
3) Burst test up to 1000 concurrent for 5 minutes to validate graceful degradation. We'll run model variants: full-precision and int8-quantized fallback to characterize trade-offs.

Probing details / measurables we need from Nimbus:
- Whitelist IPs (or allow our probe IPs): for the next 48 hours.
- A small list of representative real requests (headers + approximate token sizes) so we can mimic your streaming payloads.
- Confirm whether SYN cookies or DDoS scrubbing appliances are on the egress path during the test window.

If the initial tests show >250ms p95 first-byte, we will attach packet-level attribution and propose two mitigations: 1) move peering to a closer AZ / regional endpoint, 2) enable persistent TCP keepalive + TCP fast-open on the probe path to reduce handshake overhead.

I will produce a short report with histograms and an action matrix after the run. Ben, can you help schedule the joint troubleshooting slot on 6/20 if we need it?

—
Karthik Iyer
Staff Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
